analysis:
Examined the StartCommand.swift change (head lines ~171-180), the StatusCommand.swift change (lines 64, 102, 170-176), and the two new test files.

StartCommand now computes servedModels via advertisedModels(...) and prints a GLM wired-limit advisory to stderr from GLMWiredLimitAdvice.startNotice. It uses a hardware snapshot and live sysctl limits, runs before the local/foreground/daemon split, and reuses the already-computed runtimeCapabilities. It adds no network I/O, no config writes, and no changes to registration, attestation, authorization or encryption.

StatusCommand threads hardware into printDaemonStatus and prints a fix hint when the daemon state file's lastModelLoadError matches a Metal OOM. The message text comes from the local daemon state file, which is already printed verbatim, so there is no new disclosure. The advisory only emits a sudo sysctl command suggestion and is never executed by the CLI. Per the tests, it also emits a LaunchDaemon plist heredoc in the doctor guide for the operator to run manually. That is advisory text only, and the implementation was not supplied.

No trust boundary is crossed: no coordinator contract, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058), prefix cache (T-041) or the A-001 data paths are touched.

Tests: RegistrationWeightHashTests exercises registrationWeightHash(for:snapshotDir:verifiedWeightHashesFile:computeHash:), which caches managed GLM weight hashes in verified-weights.json and skips the full re-read on restart. The test shows invalidation after a file write. The implementation of registrationWeightHash and its change-detection granularity (size/mtime vs content) were not supplied. If the production code trusts a record keyed on weak metadata, an operator who replaces weights while preserving the metadata could register a stale hash (T-012, T-027). The operator is already the adversary for weight tampering, and the tests suggest 'any write' forces a rehash, but the exact check cannot be verified from this batch. A later pass should examine the non-test source for registrationWeightHash and the verified-weights record store, covering its file permissions and its binding to a snapshot directory.
